title: Service key lifecycle, naming, rotation and audit mapping
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: Define and implement an operationally safe lifecycle for service/API keys that integrates with RBAC v2 and audit logging. Scope includes: (1) per-scope keys (least privilege), (2) deterministic human-friendly naming conventions for keys and key-owners, (3) automated rotation workflows with grace periods and non-disruptive handoffs, (4) enforced expiry and emergency revocation, (5) a ledger/metadata surface that connects keys to principal (user/service), role bindings from RBAC v2, and audit events for forensic traceability.

Context & motivation: Existing token governance artifacts are fragmented across several initiatives. Teams report difficulty auditing long-lived keys and unclear ownership when investigating incidents. RBAC v2 introduces role bindings that must be authoritative for key scopes; audit logs need to surface key id -> role -> request mapping for compliance and incident response.

Non-goals: This ticket does not migrate existing keys automatically; migration tooling is planned in a follow-up. Does not change user-facing OAuth flows or third-party SSO federation beyond audit linkage.

Deliverables:
- API + Console surfaces: create/revoke/rotate key endpoints and UI flows that surface expiry, last rotated, and owner.
- Naming spec: prefix scheme (env/team-purpose-YYYYMMDD-unique) and validation rules.
- Rotation engine: orchestrator that can perform rolling rotations with live bind/unbind and can be run manually or on schedule.
- Audit mapping: map key id to RBAC principal and emit structured audit logs for every auth event (key_id, principal_id, role_ids, action, resource, trace_id).
- Migration plan doc for existing long-lived keys (skeleton).

Key decisions & trade-offs:
- Rotation cadence: default 90 days for service keys, 30 days for user-bound tokens. Stronger cadence increases ops overhead; we recommend 90 days but allow per-project overrides.
- Naming: human-friendly names chosen over UUID-only to simplify human ops and SRE triage; uniqueness still guaranteed via suffix. Potential leak of metadata considered low risk, aligned with existing naming for instances.
- Ledger storage: store minimal metadata (owner, created_at, last_rotated_at, expiry, scopes, origin) in encrypted configdb. Full token material never stored post-rotation. This balances auditability and secrets surface.
- Backward compatibility: provide multi-key accept during transition window and deprecation notices via Console and emails.

Implementation notes:
- API: extend /v1/keys with scope parameter supporting resource-level scoping (model:resource:action). Add rate limits and admin-only endpoints guarded by RBAC v2.
- Rotation agent: deploy as a k8s CronJob and also support on-demand via Console button + ops API. Implement pre-checks to ensure at least one valid key exists before revoking.
- Audit logs: structured JSON logs emitted to the audit pipeline (splunk/kafka); include redaction guidance for PII. Correlate key_id with trace_id for request chains.
- Console UX: show rotation status, next scheduled rotation, and a one-click emergency revoke. Add warnings when keys used cross-team (cross-tenant use).

Open questions:
- Should rotation be opt-in per service or enforced org-wide? (Initial plan: org-wide default with per-project opt-outs requiring approval.)
- How to surface cross-tenant usage metrics without leaking customer data? Need privacy review.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement API + ledger + audit hooks behind a feature flag.
2) Offer self-service console UI for new keys.
3) Run opt-in pilot with infra and platform teams.
4) Enforce org-wide defaults and start migration tooling for high-risk keys.

Success metrics:
- 100% of new service keys created after rollout follow naming and expiry rules.
- Audit events include key->principal mapping for 99.9% of authenticated requests.
- Reduction in mean-time-to-identify (MTTI) key owner during incidents by 60% for pilot teams.

Links and artifacts: See attachments for PRD, design mockups, and initial PRs.
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with Security, Platform, and Console teams. Agreed on ledger minimal schema and rotation grace window of 7 days.
2026-03-04: Design feedback from UX - add visible 'last rotated' and a small educational tooltip about rotation impact on long-running jobs.
2026-03-06: Engineering spike completed. Prototype rotation agent can perform staged swaps in dev cluster. Observability hooks added to local audit pipeline.
2026-03-09: Security review flagged concern about naming leakage for external-facing service keys; mitigation: block public-key-like names and enforce project prefix.
2026-03-10: PR created for /v1/keys extensions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4127. Requesting review from @security-team and @console-ux.
Next steps: finalize API contract, finish Console UX, add automated test coverage for rotation safety checks, schedule pilot by 2026-03-25.
